title: Bumpy ice helps these stones slide
hook: Before curling games, droplets are sprayed onto the rink to form tiny ice bumps
summary: Tiny ice bumps are part of preparing a curling rink. Properly prepared bumps reduce friction, but too many can slow the stone down.

text: You might expect a curling stone to need mirror-smooth ice to slide well.
Instead, before a game, workers spray water droplets over the rink. The droplets freeze into tiny bumps.

panels.text: Are they messing up the ice before the game?

text: The stone travels over these bumps. The photo shows ice being prepared for play.
The stone's whole base doesn't touch the ice. A hollowed-out bottom leaves a narrow ring of contact.
Properly prepared bumps reduce friction. But more isn't always better: too many bumps can slow the stone down.

panels.text: I thought they were ruining it. They're setting it up.
